key_insight: Rutile IrO2 is more stable than RuO2 because its metal–oxygen bonding has a different balance of covalent and ionic character, which can be captured by electronic structure descriptors.
engineering_relevance: These descriptors can help guide the design of durable, lower-loading OER anodes by predicting when rutile oxides will be both active and stable.
method: Compared bulk rutile IrO2 and RuO2 electronic structures.
Analyzed metal–oxygen bond strengths and their covalent/ionic contributions.
Used crystal-orbital-derived descriptors across selected MO2 systems to compare stability trends.
evidence_signal: The study reports a comparative computational analysis of bulk IrO2, RuO2, and related MO2 materials to explain their differing stabilities from electronic structure.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on bulk electronic-structure analysis, so surface reconstruction, electrolyte effects, and operating conditions may change practical catalyst stability.
paper_title: The Stability of Rutile Oxides for Oxygen Evolution Catalysis: From Mechanistic Understanding to New Descriptors
